originality.rationale: Yao and Chang arXiv:1301.5667v1 pp. 3–5 provide the centralizer lemma and an algebraically closed pair-variety classification, including its dimension p. They do not state all-arity m>=3 finite-field counts nor higher-arity dimension; the projectivized common-centralizer partition gives those new implications. Evans–Fuchs arXiv:math/0111271v1 concerns restricted powers, not tuple arithmetic. Finite external searches cannot establish absolute priority.
residual_risks: An equivalent higher-arity point-count formula might have appeared in older modular Cartan-type Lie literature under a different name.
Yao–Chang gives the essential centralizer pattern; priority attaches only to the all-arity arithmetic and dimension, not to that earlier lemma or the pair case.
